Add a backward-time basis to longitudinal sub-model formulas

Source: R/backwardTimeBasis.R
backwardTimeBasis.Rd

The backward joint model describes a biomarker given the event time \(T\). survivalTrans() adds flexibility in \(T\) itself, through terms \(|T - c|\) that are the same at every visit of a patient. Biomarkers often change instead with the time left until the event, the backward time \(u = T - s\), where \(s\) is the visit time: for example, a marker that stays flat for years and then accelerates in the last year or two before the event. A term in \(T\), \(s\) and \(T \times s\) can only describe such a trajectory as linear in \(u\).

backwardTimeBasis() adds the piecewise-linear basis \(|u - c| = |T - s - c|\), one term per cut point \(c\), to each formula. The terms are written as I(abs(years - year - c)), so they are ordinary columns of the fixed-effects design. They need no survival_variable_all/survival_trans_function entries: predictRisk(), predictLongitudinal() and simulateTrajectory() evaluate them at every integration grid point of the event time from the formula itself, using each row's visit time.

Usage

backwardTimeBasis(
  long_sub_fixed,
  cut_points,
  survival_variable = "years",
  time_variable = "year"
)

Arguments

long_sub_fixed

A fixed-effects formula, or a list of them (one per biomarker, as passed to longitudinalSub()). Each formula should already use the event time, e.g. serBilir ~ year + age + sex + years.

cut_points

A non-empty numeric vector of cut points on the backward-time scale, in the units of survival_variable. Knots where the trajectory may bend, e.g. c(0.5, 1, 2, 4) for changes concentrated in the last few years before the event.

survival_variable

Name of the event-time column ("years" in pbc3).

time_variable

Name of the visit-time column ("year" in pbc3).

Value

long_sub_fixed with the terms I(abs(survival_variable - time_variable - c)) appended to the right-hand side of each formula. A single formula in gives a single formula out, and a list keeps its names. Each formula keeps its environment.

See also

survivalTrans() for a basis in the event time itself; vignette("nonlinear-terms", package = "BJM").

Examples

backwardTimeBasis(serBilir ~ year + age + sex + years, c(1, 3))
#> serBilir ~ year + age + sex + years + I(abs(years - year - 1)) + 
#>     I(abs(years - year - 3))
#> <environment: 0x61a5bc05fc08>

long_sub_fixed <- backwardTimeBasis(
  list("serBilir" = serBilir ~ year + age + sex + years,
       "albumin"  = albumin  ~ year + age + sex + years),
  cut_points = c(1, 3, 5)
)
long_sub_fixed
#> $serBilir
#> serBilir ~ year + age + sex + years + I(abs(years - year - 1)) + 
#>     I(abs(years - year - 3)) + I(abs(years - year - 5))
#> <environment: 0x61a5bc05fc08>
#> 
#> $albumin
#> albumin ~ year + age + sex + years + I(abs(years - year - 1)) + 
#>     I(abs(years - year - 3)) + I(abs(years - year - 5))
#> <environment: 0x61a5bc05fc08>
#> 

# \donttest{
data(pbc3)
data_fit_all <- list(pbc3[pbc3$status3 == 1, ], pbc3[pbc3$status3 == 1, ])
long_fit_all <- longitudinalSub(data_fit_all, long_sub_fixed,
                                list("serBilir" = ~ year | id, "albumin" = ~ year | id))
# }
